subject: PHS
vignette: A 33-year-old woman with a history of psychological trauma presents for her first complete physical examination. The physician has completed the behavioral health screening and now prepares to begin the physical exam portion of the visit.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate statement by the physician before beginning the physical examination?

options.text: "I'll need you to undress completely now so we can get through the whole exam in one pass."
"You may signal to end the exam immediately if you experience too much physical or emotional discomfort, and a staff member can be present for support."
"This exam is routine, so there is no need for you to say anything about your history during it."
"Let's defer the entire physical exam to a future visit until you feel more comfortable here."
"I will describe each step as I perform it, and I would appreciate it if you stayed as still as possible."

explanation_correct: Trauma-informed care explicitly directs the physician to reassure patients before the physical exam that they may signal to end it immediately if they experience too much physical or emotional discomfort, and to offer the presence of additional staff for support. This gives the patient control over the encounter, which is central to avoiding retraumatization.

explanation_incorrect.A: Requiring complete undress and a fast-paced exam removes the patient's sense of control and ignores the need for the patient to be able to stop at any point.
explanation_incorrect.C: Telling the patient not to speak during the exam contradicts the directive to remain empathetic and responsive to discomfort during the encounter.
explanation_incorrect.D: Indefinitely deferring a needed exam is not the trauma-informed approach; the recommended approach is to proceed while empowering the patient to stop and offering staff support.
explanation_incorrect.E: Narrating steps and asking the patient to stay still imposes a performance expectation; the key trauma-informed element is the patient's right to end the exam immediately.

educationalObjective: Before examining a trauma survivor, reassure the patient they may end the exam immediately and offer staff presence for support.

subject: PHS
vignette: A 27-year-old man screens positive for post-traumatic stress symptoms after military deployment. He mentions that he has "never told anyone the whole story." The physician wants to explore how trauma-related symptoms are affecting his life.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate approach by the physician?

options.text: Ask permission prior to discussion and avoid invasive questions requiring the patient to describe the trauma in detail
Ask the patient to recount the full deployment events so the severity can be graded accurately
Allow the patient to determine the dose of his own medications since the physician cannot know his experience
Contact his commanding officer to obtain the unit's incident reports and reconstruct the events
Schedule the discussion for a group therapy session so he can practice disclosure among peers

explanation_correct: Trauma-informed care directs the physician to always be empathetic, to not ask invasive questions requiring the patient to describe trauma in detail, and to ask permission prior to discussion. Assessments should focus on trauma-related symptoms that interfere with social and occupational function, not on forcing a detailed narrative of the traumatic events themselves.

explanation_incorrect.B: Requesting a full recounting of the events is exactly the invasive, detailed description of trauma the patient must not be asked to provide.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ceding prescribing decisions to the patient is an abdication of the physician's role and is not part of trauma-informed care.
explanation_incorrect.D: Obtaining military incident reports to reconstruct the trauma circumvents the patient's consent to discuss it and violates the permission-first principle.
explanation_incorrect.E: Scheduling disclosure in a group setting without consent ignores the requirement to ask permission before trauma-related discussion and may expose him before he is ready.

educationalObjective: Never ask invasive questions requiring detailed trauma description; ask permission first and focus on symptoms that impair function.

subject: PHS
vignette: A clinic is redesigning its care pathway for patients with a history of psychological trauma. The leadership team adopts a framework summarized by four principles: awareness that trauma is widespread, identification of signs and symptoms in patients, integration of this knowledge into policies and procedures, and active avoidance of re-exposing patients to situations that recreate the original traumatic experience.
question: Which of the following correctly pairs each principle with its corresponding element of the trauma-informed care framework?

options.text: Realize, Recognize, Respond, Resist retraumatization — in that order
Recognize, Realize, Respond, Resist retraumatization — in that order
Realize, Respond, Recognize, Resist retraumatization — in that order
Recognize, Realize, Resist retraumatization, Respond — in that order
Realize, Recognize, Resist retraumatization, Respond — in that order

explanation_correct: The 4 R's of trauma-informed care are Realize (awareness that trauma is widespread among patients), Recognize (identification of the signs and symptoms of trauma), Respond (integrating this knowledge into policies, procedures, and practice), and Resist retraumatization (actively avoiding situations that recreate the original traumatic experience). The order described in the vignette matches Realize, Recognize, Respond, Resist retraumatization exactly.

explanation_incorrect.B: This pairing swaps the first two principles: recognizing signs and symptoms cannot come before realizing that trauma is widespread, which is the foundation of the framework.
explanation_incorrect.C: This pairing places Respond before Recognize; policies and procedures can only be integrated after the signs and symptoms of trauma are identified.
explanation_incorrect.D: This pairing inverts Realize and Recognize and also reverses Respond and Resist retraumatization; avoiding retraumatization is the final, ongoing principle, not a prerequisite for responding.
explanation_incorrect.E: This pairing correctly starts with Realize and Recognize but then reverses the final two elements: Respond (integrating knowledge into practice) precedes Resist retraumatization, not the reverse.

educationalObjective: The 4 R's of trauma-informed care are Realize, Recognize, Respond, and Resist retraumatization, in that order.
